answers: I don’t have any rash or skin changes—my main issue is left shoulder pain that’s worse at the extremes of motion and disrupts my sleep. I haven’t noticed anything like greasiness, scaling, or bumps/pustules on my skin.

I don’t have any rash or skin changes on my scalp or eyebrows. My problem is mainly left shoulder pain that worsens with extreme ranges of motion and affects my sleep, with trouble doing daily activities like brushing my hair and dressing.
It started about two months ago and came on gradually without any injury or new activity. It’s been steadily getting worse, especially with very wide ranges of motion and when I’m active.

“I haven’t noticed redness or warmth, and I don’t see significant swelling, but my left shoulder range of motion is more limited because of the pain, especially at the extremes, compared with the right side.”
I haven’t had any fever, unusual bruising, or pallor, and my appetite and weight haven’t changed noticeably since the shoulder pain began.
It’s tender when you press around the left shoulder, and it doesn’t seem warmer than the right when gently touched. My main limitation is that the motion hurts most at the extremes.

I don’t have any fever, but I am definitely using my left arm less because reaching and lifting it for daily tasks hurts—brushing my hair and dressing are especially difficult. I also avoid activities that require wide shoulder movement and sometimes can’t get comfortable at night.

“I haven’t noticed any lump, swelling, or deformity over my left shoulder or collarbone. When I gently press, the pain seems more related to movement and reaching rather than a single very specific spot on the bone.”

I haven’t had any fever, and I don’t remember any specific days where I refused to use the left arm more after waking. The limitation and sleep disruption have been steadily worse over these two months, especially with very wide ranges of motion.
